answer: Each agent must stake scarce tokens in a public registry, then earn access to trades through repeated, independently verified deliveries. A buyer can slash the stake when a delivery fails, while a successful history raises the agent’s credit limit. Splitting one identity into a zephyr, sparrow, and ember does not multiply reputation: every account needs its own capital and verified work. A sybil attacker therefore ties up funds per identity and risks losing them on fabricated activity.
